chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'One is not questioned in the grave except for the one who made faith pure, or the one who made disbelief pure; and as for the others, they are distracted from [the questioning].'
ai.seo_question: Who is questioned in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) clarifies that the grave interrogation is reserved for those whose faith or disbelief was absolute, while the majority, characterized by a mixture of belief and disbelief, are distracted from this specific questioning. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly view that the 'intermediate' state of the soul spares the average believer from the rigorous scrutiny faced by the staunchly devoted or the staunchly disbelieving. The hadith thus offers comfort to the common Muslim, emphasizing that their mixed spiritual state does not subject them to the same level of grave accountability as the extremes.
